title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 78
paragraphs: Cyrus, however, as soon as Croesus marched away after the battle that had been fought in Pteria, having learned that Croesus intended to disband his army once he had marched off, took counsel with himself and concluded that it was best for him to march to Sardis as quickly as possible, before the power of the Lydians could again be gathered together. So once he had resolved on this, he carried it out without delay, for he marched his army into Lydia with such speed that he was himself the first to announce his coming to Croesus. Then Croesus, although he had come to a great strait—since his affairs had fallen out altogether contrary to his own expectation—still proceeded to lead the Lydians out into battle. At this time there was no nation in Asia more courageous or stouter in battle than the Lydian; they fought on horseback carrying long spears, and the men were excellent horsemen.
